AAPL.rationale: Apple's fundamental health is strong: Q2 FY2026 delivered $111.18B revenue (+16.6% YoY), $2.01 EPS (+21.8% YoY), 49.3% gross margin, 32.3% operating margin, and $28.7B operating cash flow (+19.8% YoY). The balance sheet has strengthened materially with equity expanding +59.5% and debt declining -12.8% over five quarters. Services revenue hit an all-time record of $31B at ~76% gross margin, and the installed base of 2.5B+ devices with ~90% retention underpins a durable franchise. However, valuation is not compelling: P/E of 33.1x yields only 3.0%, below the 4.4% 10-year Treasury, implying a negative equity risk premium. While the stock has derated ~10 turns from its 43x peak, 33x is not cheap in absolute terms for a company whose earnings yield trails risk-free rates. ROE has compressed from 1.508 to 1.151, and the TTM data is incomplete, preventing full-year trajectory verification. The memory cost headwind (Cook's '100-year flood') and recent 6% price decline on MacBook/iPad price increases add near-term margin uncertainty. The $100B buyback authorization and R&D acceleration (+33.6% YoY) are positives but don't overcome the valuation stretch. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst) is neutral-to-slightly-negative: the memory cost shock and potential rate hikes under new Fed Chair Warsh are headwinds, while the Intel partnership and AI monetization are longer-term positives not yet confirmed. Net: solid business, fair-to-slightly-rich valuation, no compelling near-term re-rating catalyst.
